newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ retail sales trend falls in March qtr - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ retail sales trend falls in March qtr - SNZ.

text.p: The underlying trend in New Zealand retail sales fell 0.6 percent in the March quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday.
SNZ said it was the third consecutive quarter to show a decrease in the trend estimate.
After adjusting for seasonal effects and price inflation, retail sales in the quarter were estimated to have fallen by 0.8 percent over the December 1996 quarter.

In seasonally adjusted terms, retail sales for the quarter were NZ$9.5 billion, down one percent on the previous quarter. Eight of the 15 storetypes recorded falls in seasonally adjusted sales when compared with the December quarter, led by motor vehicle retailing, down 5.4 percent.

Compared to the March 1996 quarter, actual retail sales fell by two percent, or $193 million, to $9.3 billion in the March 1997 quarter. SNZ said the fall followed 20 consecutive periods of annual increases in actual retail sales.

The motor vehicle retailing storetype recorded the largest annual dollar decrease, falling by a dramatic $280 million (15.2 percent) in the year to the March 1997 quarter. The next biggest fall came from motor vehicle services, down $42 million, and clothing and softgoods outlets, down $23 million.
Total actual retail sales excluding both motor vehicle storetypes rose by $128.8 million from the March 1996 quarter to the March 1997 quarter.
The North Island recorded a 1.9 percent fall in retail sales between the March quarters of 1996 and 1997, while the South Island recorded a fall of 2.5 percent.
In the March month, actual retail sales were $3.18 billion, a fall of 4.8 percent from the March 1996 month.
After seasonal adjustment, retail sales were $3.07 billion, a fall of 3.9 percent over February 1997.
